subject.title: fix(tlon): cap SSE payload JSON.parse at 16 MiB to prevent OOM

question: Should Tlon intentionally reject and reconnect when pending SSE data or one JSON event exceeds 16 MiB?
rationale: The memory-safety repair is appropriate, but current shipped behavior has no Tlon payload ceiling and the available evidence does not define the largest legitimate Urbit event, so accepting this compatibility boundary requires owner intent.

options.title: Accept 16 MiB
options.body: Adopt 16 MiB as the supported Tlon SSE safety boundary and merge the current implementation.

options.title: Choose A Supported Ceiling
options.body: Use Urbit protocol or observed production payload evidence to select a different fixed limit and update the boundary tests.

options.title: Pause The Hard Limit
options.body: Keep the PR open until legitimate Tlon event-size expectations are established.

recommendation.title: Accept 16 MiB
recommendation.body: Adopt 16 MiB as the supported Tlon SSE safety boundary and merge the current implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the Tlon plugin and SSE client and has continued to shape its runtime boundaries, making him the clearest history-backed decision owner.
